config.title: Type Assertions, Non-null & satisfies

intro.title: Type Assertions, Non-null & satisfies
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple program that safely processes user input data, such as a name and age, using TypeScript's type safety features. You will learn to use type assertions to tell TypeScript the specific type of a value when you know more than the compiler, the non-null assertion operator to confidently access values that are not null or undefined, and the satisfies operator to ensure an expression matches a type without changing its inferred type. The main technologies are TypeScript's type system and its special syntax for assertions. This will help you write more robust and predictable code by explicitly managing types in your applications.
intro.usecase: Type assertions, non-null operators, and the satisfies operator are essential when working with external data sources like APIs or user inputs where TypeScript can't infer types automatically. For example, when building a dashboard that displays real-time analytics from a third-party API, you might use type assertions to tell TypeScript that the incoming data matches your expected chart format. In form validation scenarios, the non-null assertion operator helps safely access DOM elements after confirming they exist, while satisfies ensures configuration objects for UI components like modals or filters have the correct structure without widening types unnecessarily.

objectives: Apply type assertions to override TypeScript's inferred types
Implement non-null assertions to handle potentially undefined values
Construct type-safe objects using the satisfies operator
Configure type assertions with angle bracket and as syntax
Manipulate DOM elements using type assertions for proper type inference
Integrate satisfies operator to validate object shapes while preserving literal types
Initialize variables with explicit type assertions when TypeScript cannot infer types

steps.title: Combine all concepts in a practical example
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'processUserData' that takes a parameter 'data' of type 'string | null | undefined' and returns a processed string. Inside the function: 1) Use a non-null assertion operator to assert 'data' is not null/undefined, 2) Use a type assertion with 'as' to treat it as a string, and 3) Return a formatted string like 'Processed: ' followed by the asserted value.
steps.hint: Remember to use '!' for non-null assertion and 'as string' for type assertion. The function should handle the union type parameter appropriately.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function that demonstrates practical use of non-null assertions, type assertions, and union types together in one example.
successCriteria: The 'processUserData' function is created with: 1) A parameter of type 'string | null | undefined', 2) A non-null assertion operator '!', 3) A type assertion with 'as string', and 4) Returns a formatted string.
